citations.quote: the “arbitrage gap,” and it varies with the liquidity of the underlying securities and a variety of related costs.
ETFs typically trade within a no arbitrage zone between the underlying bid and ask prices plus the explicit costs of creation and exchange fees.

frontmatter_snapshot.summary: The creation/redemption channel pins an ETF's market price inside a no-arbitrage band NAV ± c. APs step in only when the gap exceeds round-trip cost c; c scales with underlying illiquidity, fees, and hedge cost — wider band, looser tracking.
frontmatter_snapshot.title: The ETF Creation-Redemption Arbitrage Band: Why Price Tracks NAV
